subject: System Design
title: Idempotency in Payments
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Idempotency in Payments.

hook.text: The network times out after you click pay. Did it go through? You click again. You're now charged twice. Disaster.

buildup.text: Idempotency means running the same operation twice produces the same result. Charge $10 twice? Still $10.

discovery.text: An idempotency key is sent with each request. If the server sees the same key again, it returns the original result.

twist.text: Without idempotency, retries cause duplicate operations. Networks are unreliable — retries are inevitable.

climax.text: Idempotency is not optional in payment systems. It's the difference between charging once and charging repeatedly.

punchline.text: Same key, same result — no matter how many retries.

quiz.question: What does an idempotency key prevent?
options: Duplicate charges when a payment request is retried
